propositions: The .bridge_state cache in bindings.json consumes 92% of the 1.04 GiB tickets branch due to bookkeeping fields (baseline_advanced_at and last_get_pass rotation) that are never read, causing poor git delta compression and 12.79 KB marginal cost per version.

Removing baseline_advanced_at timestamps and moving last_get_pass to a sidecar file reduces marginal cost to 1.74 KB (7.4x improvement) and halves version churn, while keeping .bridge_state committed because the reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub-hosted runners.

The existing ~1 GiB of historical .bridge_state bloat is reclaimed via a single operator-gated git fast-export/fast-import pipeline that rewrites history while preserving all commits, merges, and the current HEAD tree byte-identity.

Mixed-version read compatibility allows A2-1 (sidecar write) and A2-2 (legacy field deletion) to self-heal through max(new, legacy) logic, with descendant workflow execution and explicit host refresh replacing fixed-delay gates.

Epoch-aware union merge and writer re-cloning enforce fail-closed behavior during reclaim publication and rollback, with operator-attested quiescence confirmation (zero sessions, stopped MCP servers, disabled workflows) required before history rewrite execution.

Post-rewrite verification confirms byte-identical HEAD tree, unchanged commit/merge counts, non-resurrection (no old-tip ancestry), and sub-1 MB incremental growth from representative post-window writer commits.
